COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.actClause: AN ACT to require the New York state department of transportation, in consultation with the department of motor vehicles, the governor's traffic safety committee, local police agencies, local transportation entities in Nassau and Suffolk to conduct a study to evaluate the configuration of entrance and exit ramps, and signage at entrance ways and exits on the Southern State Parkway in Nassau and Suffolk counties to determine whether adequate safety measures exist to prevent collisions and the instance of wrong way drivers
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S3137

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to require the New York state department of
transportation, in consultation with the department of motor vehicles,
the governor's traffic safety committee, local police agencies, local
transportation entities in Nassau and Suffolk to conduct a study to
evaluate the configuration of entrance and exit ramps, and signage at
entrance ways and exits on the Southern State Parkway in Nassau and
Suffolk counties to determine whether adequate safety measures exist
to prevent collisions and the instance of wrong way drivers

 PURPOSE :

To require the Department of Transportation to evaluate the
configuration of entrance and exit ramps and signage at entrance ways
and exits on the Southern State Parkway in Nassau and Suffolk
Counties.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one of this bill requires the Department of Transportation in
consultation with the New York State Department of Motor Vehicles and
the Governor's Traffic Safety Committee, local police agencies, local
transportation entities in Nassau and Suffolk counties, and local
government stakeholders to conduct a study evaluating the
configuration of entrance and exit ramps and corresponding signage at
entrance ways and exits on the Southern State Parkway in Nassau and
Suffolk counties to determine if adequate safety measures exist. This
study will also address the feasibility of design changes to increase
safety and investigate federal funding available for highway safety
improvement projects. Further, the Department of Transportation is
authorized to conduct any hearings it deems necessary to accomplish
the purposes of this act.

Section two of this bill requires the Commissioner of Transportation
to issue a report to the Governor, the Long Island Delegation of the
Legislature, Nassau and Suffolk County Executives, and Nassau and
Suffolk County Legislatures with detailed recommendations and findings
from the study within two years of this act's effective date.

Section three of this bill provides that this act shall take effect
immediately.

 JUSTIFICATION :

The Southern State Parkway is a limited-access highway in Nassau and
Suffolk counties on Long Island, beginning in Elmont, Nassau County,
at an interchange with the Belt Parkway and Cross Island Parkway and
continuing 25.53 miles east to an interchange with the Sagtikos State
Parkway in West Islip, Suffolk County. The Parkway's entrance and exit
ramps were designed and constructed during the late 1920s, when fewer
and smaller vehicles traveled at slower speeds, making its width,
grade, and shoulder design antiquated and dangerous for modern
vehicles. Unfortunately, this has led to many fatal accidents in
Nassau and Suffolk counties due to the Parkway's outdated engineering,
the configuration of the its entrance and exit ramps, and the
corresponding signage.

Today, the Southern State Parkway is one of Long Island's most heavily
traveled roads. A recent New York State Department of Transportation
study found that the parkway has five out of ten of Long Island's most
deadly driving spots. The Department of Transportation must address
this issue by conducting a study and finding solutions to update the
antiquated design and configuration of signage and entrance and exit
ramps on the Southern State Parkway to increase driver safety and save
lives.
 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2016: S.6375 - Passed Senate

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

To be determined.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.
